questions.question: 14 men can complete a work in 15 days. If 21 men are employed, then in how many days will they complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: 14 men can complete a work in 15 days. If 21 men are employed, then in how many days will they complete the same work?
questions.solution:
14 men can complete a work in 15 days = 14 x 15 = 210

⇒ 21 men can complete a work = 210 / 21 = 10 days

questions.question: Ajeet works 4 times as fast as Sohan. If Sohan can complete a work in 20 days independently, the number of days in which Ajeet and Sohan can together finish the work is:
questions.questionHtml: Ajeet works 4 times as fast as Sohan. If Sohan can complete a work in 20 days independently, the number of days in which Ajeet and Sohan can together finish the work is:
questions.solution:
Efficiency ratio of Ajeet : Sohan = 4 : 1

So time ratio will be 1 : 4

So Ajeet takes it 20/4 = 5days

Together does in 1 day, 1/5 + 1/20 = 1/4 part

Then Ajeet and Sohan can together finish the work in 4 days.

questions.question: Ram and Shyam can complete a task in \(6\frac{2}{3}\) days and 15 days, respectively. They work together for 4 days, and then Ram leaves. In how many days after Ram leaves, will Shayam complete the remaining task alone?
questions.questionHtml: Ram and Shyam can complete a task in \(6\frac{2}{3}\) days and 15 days, respectively. They work together for 4 days, and then Ram leaves. In how many days after Ram leaves, will Shayam complete the remaining task alone?
questions.solution:
Total work = 60

Work done by Ram and Shyam in 4 days = (9 + 4) × 4 = 52

Remaining work = 60 - 52 = 8

Remaining work, B complete in = 8/4 = 2 days

questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 40 days. A can do the same job on her own in 60 days. How long will B take to do the three-fourth of the same work all alone?
questions.questionHtml: A and B together can finish a job in 40 days. A can do the same job on her own in 60 days. How long will B take to do the three-fourth of the same work all alone?
questions.solution:
Efficiency of A = 120/60 = 2  unit/day.

Efficiency of B =  Efficiency of (A +B) - Efficiency of A  ⇒ ( 3 - 2) = 1 unit/day.

3/4 of the Total work = 3/4 × 120 = 90 units.

No. of days B alone takes ⇒ 90/1 = 90 days.

questions.question: A can finish a work in 20 days and B can finish the same work in 25 days. They began together, but B left the work after 5 days. How many more days will A take to finish the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a work in 20 days and B can finish the same work in 25 days. They began together, but B left the work after 5 days. How many more days will A take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Short Trick:

Total work = 100

Work done by A and B in 5 days = (5 + 4) × 5 = 45

Remaining work = 100 – 45 = 55

∴ Remaining work, A complete in = 55/5 = 11 days

questions.question: Fifteen persons working 12 hours a day earn Rs. 18,000 per week. How many rupees will 18 persons working 9 hours a day earn per week?
questions.questionHtml: Fifteen persons working 12 hours a day earn Rs. 18,000 per week. How many rupees will 18 persons working 9 hours a day earn per week?
questions.solution:
15 persons x 12 hours/day x 7 days = 1260 hours

Earnings per hour = 18000 / 1260 = 14.29 Rs/hour

18 persons x 9 hours/day x 7 days = 1134 hours

Total earnings = 1134 hours x 14.29 Rs/hour = 16198.86 ≈ 16200 Rs

questions.question: 20 workers can paint 24 walls in 36 days. In how many days can 30 workers paint 20 walls?
questions.questionHtml: 20 workers can paint 24 walls in 36 days. In how many days can 30 workers paint 20 walls?
questions.solution:
If 20  workers paints 24 walls in 36 days

Then, 1 worker can paint 24 walls in = 36 × 20 days

And , 1 worker can paint 1 wall in = (36 × 20)/24 = 720/24 = 30 days

Therefore, 30 workers can paint 1 wall in = 30/30 days = 1 day

Hence, 30 workers can paint 20 walls in = 1 × 20 days = 20 days

questions.question: 24 persons working 8 hours a day can complete 2 units of a work in 10 days. How many persons are required to complete 4 units of that work, if they work 6 hours a day for 16 days?
questions.questionHtml: 24 persons working 8 hours a day can complete 2 units of a work in 10 days. How many persons are required to complete 4 units of that work, if they work 6 hours a day for 16 days?
questions.solution:
m1 d1 h1 w2 = m2 d2 h2 w1

⇒ 24 × 10 × 8 × 4 = m2 × 16 × 6 × 2

∴ m2 = 40

questions.question: Eight labourers working 10 hours a day completed a work in 18 days. If only 5 labourers are working, then in how many hours a day should they work to finish the work in 24 days?
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->Eight labourers working 10 hours a day completed a work in 18 days. If only 5 labourers are working, then in how many hours a day should they work to finish the work in 24 days?
questions.solution:
Given:

Number of labourers working initially = 8

Hours per day worked initially = 10

Days taken initially = 18

Number of labourers working later = 5

Days taken later = 24

Formula Used:

Total Work = Number of Labourers × Hours per day × Days

Calculation:

Total Work (initial) = 8 × 10 × 18

Total Work (initial) = 1440 hours

Total Work (later) = 5 × Hours per day × 24

Since Total Work (initial) = Total Work (later)

1440 = 5 × Hours per day × 24

⇒ Hours per day = 1440 / (5 × 24)

⇒ Hours per day = 1440 / 120

⇒ Hours per day = 12

The correct answer is option 4 i.e. 12 hours.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 8 days, while B can do it in 7 days. If they work at it alternately beginning with A, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 8 days, while B can do it in 7 days. If they work at it alternately beginning with A, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM of (8, 7) = 56 unit

Efficiency of A = 56 / 8 = 7 unit / day, Efficiency of B = 56 / 7 = 8 unit / day

Now, it is said that they work on alternate days starting with A

In 2 days total work done is (7 + 8) = 15 unit

⇒ In (2 × 3) = 6 days work done is (15 × 3) = 45 unit

On the 7th day A will work, so the total work done is (45 + 7) = 52 unit

Remaining work = (56 - 52) = 4 unit to be done by B

So, B will do the remaining 4 units of work in (4 / 8) = 1/2 days

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 7 days and B can complete the same work in 12 days. A and B worked together for 3 days. C alone completed the remaining work in 9 days will C take to complete the same work entirely?
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a piece of work in 7 days and B can complete the same work in 12 days. A and B worked together for 3 days. C alone completed the remaining work in 9 days will C take to complete the same work entirely?
questions.solution:
Given:

A's 1 day's work = 1/7

B's 1 day's work = 1/12

Calculation:

(A + B)'s 1 day's work = 1/7 + 1/12 = 19/84

(A + B)'s 3 days work = 3 × 19/84 = 19/28

Remaining work = 1 - 19/28 = 9/28

Number of days in which C alone can complete work = 28/9 × 9 = 28 days

∴ C alone can complete work in 28 days. 

Alternate MethodLet the total work be 84.(LCM of 7 and 12)

Efficiency of A = 84/7 = 12

Efficiency of B = 84/12 = 7

The work of A + B in 3 days = 19 × 3 = 57

Remaining work = 84 - 57 = 27

Efficiency of C = 27/9 = 3

Time required for C = 84/3 = 28 days

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 12 days and 16 days, respectively. If they work together for 6 days, then the fraction of the work left is ________.
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a work in 12 days and 16 days, respectively. If they work together for 6 days, then the fraction of the work left is ________.
questions.solution:
Work done by A in 1 day = 1/12, Work done by B in 1 day = 1/16

Work done by both in 1 day = 1/12 + 1/16 = 7/48

Work done by both in 6 days = 6 × 7/48 = 7/8

Fraction of work left = 1 - 7/8 = 1/8

questions.question: Abraham can complete a work in 9 days, while Andrew can complete the same work in 6 days. In how many days can they complete the work if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: Abraham can complete a work in 9 days, while Andrew can complete the same work in 6 days. In how many days can they complete the work if they work together?

The efficiency of Abraham is ⇒ 18 / 6 = 3 unit

Again, the Efficiency of Andrew  is, ⇒ 18 / 9 = 2 unit

Total Efficiency, ⇒ 3 + 2  = 5 unit

The number of days required is, ⇒ 18 /5 = \(3{3 \over 5}\) days

questions.question: The efficiency of A, B and C are in the ratio 5 ∶ 6 ∶ 9 Working together, they can complete a work in 18 days. In how many days can B alone complete 25% of that work?
questions.questionHtml: The efficiency of A, B and C are in the ratio 5 ∶ 6 ∶ 9 Working together, they can complete a work in 18 days. In how many days can B alone complete 25% of that work?
questions.solution:
The efficiencies ratios of A, B and C = 5 ∶ 6 ∶ 9

Total work = (5 + 6 + 9) × 18 = 20 × 18 = 360

25% of the total work = 360 × 25/100 = 90

B alone can complete the 25% of the total work = 90/6 = 15 days

questions.question: Jason can do a piece of work alone In 23.4 days. while Rafique can do the same piece of work alone in 39 days. In how many days can the duo complete the same work if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: Jason can do a piece of work alone In 23.4 days. while Rafique can do the same piece of work alone in 39 days. In how many days can the duo complete the same work if they work together?
questions.solution:
Given :

Jason can do a piece of work alone = 23.4 days.

Rafique can do the same piece of work alone = 39

Concept used :

Number of days to complete work = Total work /Efficiency

Formula used :

Efficiency = Total work / no. of days

Calculation : 

Let as the total work = 23.4× 39 = 912.6

Efficiency of Jason = 912.6 / 23.4 = 39

Efficiency of Rafique = 912.6 / 39 = 23.4

Efficiency of Jason and Rafique = 39 + 23.4 = 62.4

⇒ Number of days to complete work = Total work /Efficiency

⇒ Number of days to complete work = 912.6 / 62.4

⇒ 14.625

Hence, the correct option (2).

questions.question: R and S can finish a work in 10 days, S and T can finish it in 12 days and T and R can finish in 8 days. In how many days will the work be finished if they all work simultaneously?
questions.questionHtml: R and S can finish a work in 10 days, S and T can finish it in 12 days and T and R can finish in 8 days. In how many days will the work be finished if they all work simultaneously?
questions.solution:
Given: r + s = 1/10, s + t = 1/12, t + r = 1/8

Add: 2(r + s + t) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8 ⇒ 2(r + s + t) = 37/120

r + s + t = 37/240 ⇒ Days required = \(\frac{240}{37}\) Days

questions.question: The efficiency of A is thrice as that of B and efficiency of B is twice as that of C. If B alone can finish a work in 15 days, in how many days A and C together will complete that work?
questions.questionHtml: The efficiency of A is thrice as that of B and efficiency of B is twice as that of C. If B alone can finish a work in 15 days, in how many days A and C together will complete that work?
questions.solution:
Let the efficiency of C be x, then

Efficiency of B = x × 2 = 2x

Efficiency of A = 2x × 3 = 6x

Efficiency ratio of A, B and C = x ∶ 2x ∶ 6x = 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 6

Total work = 2 × 15 = 30

A and C together will complete the whole work in = 30/(1 + 6) = 30/7 = 4\(\frac{2}{7}\)

questions.question: A, B and C can separately do a work in 6, 10 and 15 days respectively. They started to work together but C left after 2 days. In how many days will the remaining work be finished?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can separately do a work in 6, 10 and 15 days respectively. They started to work together but C left after 2 days. In how many days will the remaining work be finished?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM of (6, 10, 15) = 30 unit,

Efficiency of A = 30/6 = 5 units, efficiency of B = 30/10 = 3 units, efficiency of C = 30/15 = 2 units

Remaining work after they worked for 2 days together = 30 - (5 + 3 + 2) × 2 = 10 unit, Remaining work will be finished in = 10 ÷ (5 + 3) = \(1\frac{1}{4}\) days

questions.question: X can complete a work in 5 days and Y in 10 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is:
questions.questionHtml: X can complete a work in 5 days and Y in 10 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Efficiency(X) = 1/5

Efficiency(Y) = 1/10

Solution:

Efficiency(X+Y) in 2 days = 2 x (1/5 + 1/10) = 6/10 = 3/5

Hence, the work left = 1 - 3/5 = 2/5

The fraction of work left is 2/5.

questions.question: X, Yand Z can do a work in 24 days. 5 days and 12 days, respectively. In how many days can they do the same work if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: X, Yand Z can do a work in 24 days. 5 days and 12 days, respectively. In how many days can they do the same work if they work together?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken by X to do the work = 24 days.

Time taken by Y to do the work = 5 days.

Time taken by Z to do the work = 12 days.

Formula used:

Work rate = 1 / Time taken

Combined work rate = Work rate of X + Work rate of Y + Work rate of Z

Time taken when working together = 1 / Combined work rate

Calculation:

Work rate of X = 1 / 24

Work rate of Y = 1 / 5

Work rate of Z = 1 / 12

Combined work rate = (1 / 24) + (1 / 5) + (1 / 12)

To add the fractions, find the LCM of 24, 5, and 12, which is 120.

⇒ Combined work rate = (5 / 120) + (24 / 120) + (10 / 120)

⇒ Combined work rate = (5 + 24 + 10) / 120

⇒ Combined work rate = 39 / 120

Time taken when working together = 1 / (39 / 120)

⇒ Time taken when working together = 120 / 39

⇒ Time taken when working together = 3(1/13) days

∴ The correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: A alone can make a table in 30 days while B alone can make it in 15 days. B started the work alone and worked for 8 days. In how many days A alone can finish the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: A alone can make a table in 30 days while B alone can make it in 15 days. B started the work alone and worked for 8 days. In how many days A alone can finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Rate of A = 1/30 table/day, Rate of B = 1/15 table/day.

Work done by B = Rate × Time = (1/15) × 8 = 8/15 table.

Remaining work = 1 - 8/15 = 7/15 table.

Time taken by A to finish the remaining work = Work / Rate = (7/15) / (1/30) = 14 days.

questions.question: A can finish a work in 25 days, and B can do the same work in 15 days. B worked for 10 days and left the job. A alone can finish the remaining work in how many days?
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a work in 25 days, and B can do the same work in 15 days. B worked for 10 days and left the job. A alone can finish the remaining work in how many days?

A will do the remaining work = (75 - 50)/3 =  8(1/3) days

questions.questionHtml: Raju, Sunil and Vishal can separately finish a work in 20, 30 and 40 days, respectively. In how many days Raju can finish the work, if he is assisted by Sunil and Vishal on alternate days, starting with Sunil?

D = 72/5 = \(14 \frac{2}{5}\) days

questions.question: A can finish a task in 45 days and B can finish the same task in 30 days. They work together for 3 days and then A leaves. In how many days will B finish the remaining task?
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a task in 45 days and B can finish the same task in 30 days. They work together for 3 days and then A leaves. In how many days will B finish the remaining task?
questions.solution:
Given:

A can finish a task in 45 days

B can finish the same task in 30 days

(A + B) work together for 3 days.

Concept used:

If a person does work in 'n' days, then one day work will be (1/n) part of the total work.

Calculation:

A's one day work = 1/45 part of the total work

B's one day work = 1/30 part of the total work

Worked by both for one day's work = (1/45) + (1/30)

⇒ (2 + 3)/90

⇒ 5/90

⇒ 1/18 part of the total work.

Now Worked by them for 3 days = (1/18) × 3

⇒ 1/6 part of the total work

Now remaining work = 1 - (1/6)

⇒ (6 - 1)/6

⇒ 5/6 part of the total work

But B completes a work = 30 days

The remaining work (5/6) part will be completed by B = (30) × (5/6)

⇒ 5 × 5

⇒ 25 days.

∴ The remaining work, B will finish in 25 days.

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. They worked together for 4 days after which B was replaced by C and the remaining work was completed by A and C in the next 4 days. In how many days will C alone complete 50% of the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. They worked together for 4 days after which B was replaced by C and the remaining work was completed by A and C in the next 4 days. In how many days will C alone complete 50% of the same work?
questions.solution:
Efficiency of A = 36/12 = 3 units a day, Efficiency of B = 36/18 = 2 units a day

Let the efficiency of C be P units per day.4 × (3 + 2) + 4 × (3 + P) = 36 ⇒ 20 + 12 + 4P = 36 ⇒ P =  1

The time taken by C to complete 50% of the work  ⇒ (50% × 36)/1 = 18 days

questions.question: If Anju is 30% more efficient than Bitt, then how much time will they take, working together, to complete a job which Anju alone could have done in 23 days?
questions.questionHtml: If Anju is 30% more efficient than Bitt, then how much time will they take, working together, to complete a job which Anju alone could have done in 23 days?
questions.solution:
Anju is 30% more efficient than Bitt, let the efficiency of Anju = 10a, then efficiency of Bitt = 13a

So, total work = 13a × 23 ⇒ 299a

Now, If they both work then time = 299a/(13a + 10a) ⇒ 299a/23a ⇒ 299/23 ⇒ 13 days

questions.question: Ramu can build a wall alone in 15 days, while Ravan can build it alone in 10 days. Ramu worked for 5 days. Then Ravan joined Ramu for the next 3 days. How many more days could Ramu take to build the remaining wall?
questions.questionHtml: Ramu can build a wall alone in 15 days, while Ravan can build it alone in 10 days. Ramu worked for 5 days. Then Ravan joined Ramu for the next 3 days. How many more days could Ramu take to build the remaining wall?
questions.solution:
Given:

Ramu can build a wall alone in = 15 days

Ravan can build it alone = 10 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

Let the can complete the remaining work in X days.

One day work of Ramu = \({1\over15}\)

One day work of Ravan = \({1\over10}\)

5 days' work of Ramu = \({5\over15}={1\over3}\)

Ramu and Ravan worked for 3 days together. 

3 days' work of Ramu and Ravan together = \({3\over15}+{3\over10}={1\over5}+{3\over10}={10+15\over50}={25\over50}={1\over2}\)

The remaining work = \({1-{({1\over3}+{1\over2}})}={1-({2+3\over 6})}=1-{5\over6}={6-5\over6}={1\over6}\)

The remaining work completed by Ramu = \({{1\over6}\over{1\over15}}={15\over6}=2.5\ days\)

∴ The required result will be 2.5 days.

questions.question: A alone can complete a work in 20 days with full efficiency. If the efficiency of A decreases by 20 percent, then A alone can do the same work in how many days?
questions.questionHtml: A alone can complete a work in 20 days with full efficiency. If the efficiency of A decreases by 20 percent, then A alone can do the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
If the efficiency of A decreases by 20 percent, the new efficiency = 80% of the original efficiency = 0.8 Efficiency

As Time is inversely proportional to Efficiency, new time = original time/new efficiency = 20 days/0.8 = 25 days

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 80 days and 96 days, respectively. They completed the work in 32 days with the help of C, How many days will C take to complete the entire work alone?
questions.questionHtml: A and B complete a work in 80 days and 96 days, respectively. They completed the work in 32 days with the help of C, How many days will C take to complete the entire work alone?
questions.solution:
Given:

Days taken by A = 80 

Days taken by B = 96 

Days taken by A, B and C together = 32 

Formula used:

No of days taken = Work/ Efficiency per day 

Calculation:

Let the total work be = 1 

Work done be A per day = 1/80 

Work done by B per day = 1/96 

Work done by A, B and C per day = 1/32 

⇒ Work done by only C per day = 1/32 - 1/80 - 1/96 

⇒ (15 - 6 - 5)/480 = 4/480 

⇒ 1/120 

No of days taken by C = 1 ÷ 1/120 = 120 

∴ C will take 120 days to complete the entire work alone. 

Alternate Method By LCM Method 

Let the total work be the LCM of 80, 96 and 32 as the common multiple. 

Work done by C in one day = 15 - 6 - 5 = 4 

∴ No of days taken by C alone = 480/4 = 120

questions.question: Rahul alone can complete a work in 10 days and Sonu alone can complete the same work in 15 days. If they work together for 4 days, then what part of total work is left?
questions.questionHtml: Rahul alone can complete a work in 10 days and Sonu alone can complete the same work in 15 days. If they work together for 4 days, then what part of total work is left?
questions.solution:
Combined work rate per day = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6

Now, let's calculate the work done by Rahul and Sonu together in 4 days:

Work done in 4 days = (Combined work rate per day) × (Number of days they work together)

Work done in 4 days = (1/6) × 4 = 4/6 = 2/3

This means that they have completed 2/3 of the total work in 4 days.

Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3
